> KAI (Kinetic Adaptive Interface) is a modular desktop robotic arm designed to make physical computer interactions more accessible and adaptable. Instead of being a conventional pick-and-place robot, KAI is designed as a physical interface for controlling and repositioning everyday devices and objects on a desk. A combination of servo-driven joints and accessible physical controls will let users move the arm between positions without needing precise manual manipulation. The first version will focus on a compact multi-joint arm with a modular end-effector, allowing different attachments such as a phone holder, camera mount, or other lightweight desk accessories to be swapped onto the arm. What makes KAI mine is the focus on accessibility and human-computer interaction: the goal isn't just to make a robot that moves, but to explore how a physical, reconfigurable interface can give people more intuitive control over their workspace.
